message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price for gold today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check a reputable financial news site or a dedicated precious‑metal platform such as:

| Source | Typical update frequency | How to view |
|--------|--------------------------|-------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Live ticker, updated every few seconds | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” |
| **Kitco** | Live price chart, updated every minute | Visit kitco.com/price-charts |
| **Reuters** | Live ticker, updated every few seconds | Search “Gold” |
| **Investing.com** | Live price, updated every minute | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” |
| **NYMEX (COMEX)** | Futures prices, updated at market close | Check the COMEX website |

If you need a quick reference, most major sites quote the spot price in U.S. dollars per troy ounce.  As of the last publicly available data (late 2023–early 2024), gold was trading roughly in the **$1,800–$1,950 per ounce** range, but the price can fluctuate by several dollars within a single trading day.

**Tip:** If you’re looking for the exact price at a specific time, use a live ticker or a financial app that shows real‑time commodity prices.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the gold price today in USA?" They want the current gold price. We cannot browse the internet. We can provide approximate or typical price, but we should note that we don't have real-time data. We can suggest checking reliable sources like Bloomberg, Kitco, etc. We can give a typical range. We should not fabricate. So answer: "I don't have real-time data, but as of last known data, gold was around $X per ounce." But we don't know the exact. We can say "As of the last available data, gold was around $1,950 per ounce." But we should mention that it's approximate. Provide guidance.
